criterion_notes.c1: Examines urban household/community water supply sources and water access disparities across five Kenyan towns (Kisumu, Nakuru, Lodwar, Wajir, Msambweni) alongside aquifer hydrogeology and groundwater quality.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: YES — reviews national water legislation and strategies (Water Act 2002 and 2016, NWRMS, NWSS, NWMP 2030) and five County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs) regarding groundwater governance and planning. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: NO — focuses on macro-level groundwater resource planning, aquifer characterisation gaps, and national-to-county strategy alignment to propose a conceptual planning framework, rather than examining any rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing access).
criterion_notes.c3: Combines hydrogeological fieldwork (geological mapping, geophysical surveys, water-quality compilation), descriptive recalculation of 2009 Kenya Census water-source proportions across five towns, and a critical document review of national water strategies and five CIDPs, though it conducts no empirical test or socio-legal analysis linking a governance mechanism to service access.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports descriptive statistics on household water supply sources (piped into dwelling, piped, borehole, shallow well, spring, vended water, surface water) from the 2009 Census and secondary figures on per capita daily water use and nonrevenue water.
criterion_notes.c5: Although the five case-study towns and descriptive census water-source outcomes are identifiable, there is no identifiable rule-type legal/administrative exposure or empirical study design linking a governance exposure to household/community service access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is published in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: The objective was to consider governance and management solutions that could promote water security for urban towns in Kenya through the sustainable use of groundwater in the context of its complex hydrogeology, water access disparities, competing uses and future risks.

The in force national and county water policies, strategies, and plans for the case study areas were critically reviewed. The status of aquifer knowledge, water access disparities, competing uses, and risks was evaluated from critical literature reviews and data compilation, fieldwork, and analysis of indicator datasets from the Kenya 2009 census.

While households receiving piped water supply into dwellings rely on it almost solely for all domestic water requirements, those living in informal settlements or low-income urban areas rely on a wider range of water sources such as boreholes, springs and shallow wells that have different quality and prices for different domestic uses including drinking, cooking, and washing
None of them mention NWMP 2030, and only the Nakuru CIDP alludes to the development of a county water master plan.

raw_response.exposure: Macro-level national and county water resource strategies and planning documents (Water Act 2002 and 2016, NWRMS, NWSS, NWMP 2030, and five County Integrated Development Plans) and hydrogeological aquifer characteristics; no rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing service access
raw_response.outcome: Descriptive proportions of urban populations accessing water supply sources (2009 Census), secondary per capita daily water use and nonrevenue water figures, and aquifer transmissivity and water-quality parameters
raw_response.population_and_sample: Five urban towns in Kenya (Kisumu City, Nakuru, Lodwar, Wajir, and Msambweni; derived 2009 Census ward/constituency populations of 439,009, 298,254, 54,549, 51,729, and 22,633 persons, respectively) and their surrounding regional aquifers
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure). This Hydrogeology Journal report synthesises regional hydrogeology and groundwater quality across five Kenyan towns, tabulates descriptive 2009 Census water-source proportions and secondary water-use figures, and reviews macro-level national water strategies (Water Act 2002/2016, NWRMS, NWSS, NWMP 2030) and County Integrated Development Plans to propose a conceptual groundwater planning framework. Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope clarification, it does not examine any rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing household or community water service access, nor does it empirically evaluate the relationship between any governance rule and service access outcomes.
raw_response.study_design: Multi-town hydrogeological synthesis, descriptive secondary 2009 census compilation, and policy document review
